# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier, changes which command to run, or adds a new place that reports an existing failure, check every place that already reports it (status, doctor, enable, help text) so they all give the same fix. Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one, or one command prints the same failure twice with different fixes.
- When a test plants a failure to cover an error branch, make sure an earlier step doesn't fail first; otherwise the assertion passes without ever running that branch.
- Select an agent's final report by a marker it carries (such as the contract line), not by its position in the event stream; a trailing tool call or an empty message ID moves a position-based boundary.
- When code keeps state so a later run can retry, test the retry itself. A test that checks the kept state against the same expression the code uses would pass even if that expression were wrong.
- When decoding user-editable JSON into maps or pointers, skip null elements before writing to them; `[null]` decodes to a nil map and a write panics.
- Review a PR that is behind main against current main, not its own base: build both and run the same repro. Its tests pass on its old base even when keeping its side of a conflict would undo a fix merged since.
- When wiring user config into a new path, test it with a broken config too. A user rule that silently fails to load leaks the same way as one that was never wired.
- Make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against, not on a whole class of errors. A refusal on any settings error blocks unrelated cases and pushes users toward a less safe escape hatch, such as an unredacted `--raw` bundle.
- Read the Trail's current description and resolved findings before drafting review comments. The trail description can be newer than the PR description and may already list known follow-ups, which turns "you missed this" into a question about scale or timing.
- When a PR claims corpus validation, check what the corpus contained, and test on inputs from outside it, such as other languages and other codebases. A corpus drawn from one codebase can pass while common idioms elsewhere break.

    fix(trailers): align the trailer writer with the final-block grammar
    
    appendTrailerLine trimmed leading whitespace before classifying the final

    it on raw lines, still requiring a blank line above the paragraph so a

`AppendCheckpointTrailer` can emit a trailer the final-block parser (and git) reject [OPEN] by MuskanPaliwal
## Summary

`trailers.appendTrailerLine` (the writer behind `AppendCheckpointTrailer` and `AppendOPFAppliedTrailer`) and `trailers.finalTrailerBlock` (the reader behind the strict `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock` / `ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock` parsers introduced in #2253) implement two different grammars for "is this paragraph a trailer block". When a commit message ends with an indented checkpoint-shaped line, the writer joins a real trailer onto that paragraph without a separating blank line, producing a message in which **neither our strict readers nor git itself** can see the trailer that was just appended. The CLI reports success while every downstream hook silently ignores the commit.

The reader's grammar matches git's; the writer is the buggy side.

## The grammar divergence

**Writer** (`cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`, `appendTrailerLine`): to decide whether the message already ends in a trailer block, it takes the last non-comment line and tests `IsTrailerLine(strings.TrimSpace(line))`. The `TrimSpace` means an indented line like `␣␣Entire-Checkpoint: A` — which is *not* a trailer to git — passes the check. It then walks upward, again trimming each line, until it finds a blank line, and concludes "trailer block present, join directly".

**Reader** (`finalTrailerBlock`): isolates the final paragraph and accepts it only if every line is either a real trailer line (`IsTrailerLine` on the **raw** line — leading whitespace fails the `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*: ` regex) or an indented continuation *of a preceding trailer*. An indented line at the top of the paragraph has nothing to continue, so the entire paragraph is rejected and the parsers return nothing. This intentionally mirrors git, which treats an indented line after a trailer as a continuation of that trailer's value, never as a new trailer.

So the writer's membership test is strictly looser than the reader's, and the looseness is load-bearing: it changes where the writer places the new trailer.

## Reproduction

Start from a commit message whose final paragraph is an indented checkpoint-shaped line — for example one pasted from attach's own non-interactive hint, which prints the trailer with a two-space indent (`Copy to your commit message to attach:\n\n  Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`):

```
Message

Body.

  Entire-Checkpoint: <A>
```

`AppendCheckpointTrailer(msg, B)` classifies the final paragraph as an existing trailer block and joins without a blank line:

```
Message

Body.

  Entire-Checkpoint: <A>
Entire-Checkpoint: <B>
```

Verification against git, which is the authority here:

```console
$ git interpret-trailers --parse < joined.txt
$                                              # zero trailers — git rejects the whole paragraph
$ git interpret-trailers --parse < separated.txt
Entire-Checkpoint: <B>                         # same message with a blank line before B
```

`ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock` returns the same verdicts as git on both shapes. A writer/reader roundtrip test (`AppendCheckpointTrailer` → `ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`) fails on the space- and tab-indented cases.

## User-visible failure chain

1. `promptAmendCommit` (`cmd/entire/cli/attach.go`) builds the new message with `trailers.AppendCheckpointTrailer`, runs `git commit --amend`, and prints `Amended commit <hash> with Entire-Checkpoint: <B>`.
2. PostCommit (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`) parses HEAD's message with `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock`, finds nothing, and takes the no-trailer path: the commit is treated as mid-turn — no checkpoint linkage, no condensation. Same for the commit-msg validation and `parseCheckpointFromCommitMessageFile`, so the prepare-commit-msg path (`addCheckpointTrailer` delegates to the same writer) is equally affected.
3. Attach's idempotence check (`ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock` over HEAD before amending) also can't see B, so re-running attach appends the same trailer **again** into the still-rejected paragraph. The failure is self-reinforcing rather than self-correcting.

The net effect inverts #2253's intent at this one seam: that PR ensures body text can't *grant* checkpoint authority; this bug makes a legitimately granted trailer *lose* authority while reporting success.

## Secondary inconsistency (same root cause)

A valid trailer block whose last line is an indented continuation, e.g.

```
Message

Signed-off-by: Test User <test@example.com>
 continuation text
```

makes the writer conclude "no trailer block" (the trimmed last line isn't a trailer) and insert a blank line, splitting what git considers one block into two. B is still recognized (it forms its own final block), so this is cosmetic — but it falls out of the same divergent grammar and is fixed by the same change.

`AppendOPFAppliedTrailer` shares `appendTrailerLine`, so it carries the same latent shape; in practice v1 checkpoint messages are generated entirely by Entire's own formatters and can't naturally end in an indented pseudo-trailer, so no OPF-specific behavior change is expected beyond inheriting the fix.

## Proposed fix

Single source of truth for the grammar:

1. Extract `finalTrailerBlock`'s classification loop into a shared `isTrailerBlock(lines []string) bool`: at least one trailer line, every line either a trailer or an indented continuation of a preceding trailer.
2. Rewrite `appendTrailerLine` to collect the final non-comment paragraph as **raw** lines (comment-line skipping preserved for the prepare-commit-msg template case) and join only when `isTrailerBlock(paragraph)` holds **and** a blank line separates the paragraph from the content above. The blank-line requirement preserves the existing guard that keeps a trailer-shaped subject line (`fix: bug` matches the trailer regex) from having the trailer glued onto it.

For the reproduction above, B then starts a fresh final paragraph:

I reviewed [entireio/cli#2259](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2259) without editing anything. The code change is correct, but the PR isn't ready for review yet. It conflicts with main in 6 files, it's out of sync with #2253's newest commit (`7be8499d4`), its CI never ran, and its description no longer matches the code. I recommend folding it into #2253 and rebasing once.

**Worktree:** clean. Local HEAD `ef07a954a` matches the PR head.

## Brief

**What it does for users.** `entire checkpoint attach` and the commit hooks add an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer to commit messages. In one edge case they put it where neither git nor Entire's stricter readers can find it. The trigger is a message whose last paragraph is an indented trailer-like line, for example one pasted from attach's own indented hint. `attach` then prints "Amended commit … with Entire-Checkpoint", but the commit isn't actually linked, and re-running it adds the trailer again.

**Why it exists.** #2253 tightens the reader: only a real final trailer block counts, matching git's rules. The writer still used the older, looser rule. #2259 makes the writer follow the same rule.

**How it works.**
- The reader's check moves into a shared `isTrailerBlock` (`trailers.go:319`).
- The writer only joins the new trailer onto the last paragraph if that paragraph passes the check and has a blank line above it (`trailers.go:243-264`). Otherwise it starts a new block.
- The latest commit also stops the writer from skipping `#` lines; they now count as ordinary text.

**Performance, compatibility, data, risk.**
- Performance: unchanged, a single pass over the message lines.
- Compatibility: some messages now get the trailer in a separate final block instead of joined onto an existing block. Every message the writer produces is now one the readers accept.
- Data: no stored data or formats change.
- Risk: low in the code itself, high in the merge logistics (see finding 1).

**Uncertain.** I couldn't build or test the PR merged with current main, because it conflicts.

## Findings (most severe first)

1. **The stack is out of sync with #2253, and both PRs conflict with main.**
   - #2259 carries old copies of #2253's first two commits. It doesn't include #2253's newest commit `7be8499d4` ("simplify commit message parsing"), which changes the same reader functions in `trailers.go` plus `manual_commit_hooks.go`. Compared against #2253's head, this PR's diff undoes that commit.
   - The PR body's line "once #2253 lands, the diff collapses to one commit" is no longer true without a rebase.
   - `git merge-tree` against current main shows the same conflicts for both PRs in:
     - `attach.go`
     - `explain.go`
     - `manual_commit_hooks.go`
     - `trailers.go`
     - `manual_commit_migration.go` and its test, which main deleted (modify/delete conflict)
   - Main has also changed the code this PR depends on:
     - It moved attach's amend into `attach_confirm.go:200`.
     - It added `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` and `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer`; the latter calls this writer.
     - `HasOPFApplied` now trims whitespace on each line.

2. **#2253 must not merge without this PR.** The writer/reader mismatch only appears once #2253's stricter reader is in. On main today, Entire's readers use an unanchored regex that still finds the appended trailer; only `git interpret-trailers` misses it. Merging #2253 alone would ship the bug that #2259 fixes.

3. **The PR description and issue #2256 are out of date after `ef07a954a`.**
   - The body names `TestAppendCheckpointTrailerRecognizedByFinalBlockParser`, which that commit removed. Its check now lives inline at `trailers_test.go:77`.
   - It says "five subtests fail"; against the current tests it's four.
   - It says "review only the last commit", but the PR now has two commits of its own.
   - It describes the writer as using the "final non-comment paragraph". The issue's proposed fix also says comment-skipping is kept. The code now does the opposite.

4. **`ef07a954a` changes behavior without explaining why.** The commit has no body. Treating `#` lines as text looks right:
   - In committed messages (`attach`, the OPF rewrite) and in `-m`/`-F` messages, `#` lines are content. Main's `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer` documents the same rule.
   - The writer can't know `core.commentChar`.
   - I confirmed with real git that its editor and amend templates always put a blank line before the comment block, so the editor and amend flows decide the same as before.

   That reasoning belongs in the commit message. The two PR commits could also be squashed into one during the rebase.

5. **Nit:** the doc comment on `AppendCheckpointTrailer` (`trailers.go:266-268`) still describes the old joining rule.

I found no correctness bugs in the code change itself. The writer only joins onto a paragraph the reader already accepts, and adding one more trailer line keeps that paragraph valid.

## Verification (all read-only)

- **Before/after:** I swapped in the pre-fix `trailers.go` without touching the repo (Go's `-overlay` flag). 4 subtests fail with the old writer and all pass with HEAD.
- **Random messages:** over 20,000 random messages, HEAD's writer had 0 misses by our reader and 0 of 500 sampled misses by real `git interpret-trailers --parse`. The pre-fix writer with #2253's reader had 1,214 reader misses and 17/500 git misses.
- **Tests and lint on HEAD:** the trailers tests pass, focused strategy tests pass (282s), focused attach/explain tests pass, and lint on the trailers package reports 0 issues.
- **Not run:** `mise run check`, integration tests, and the canary. The branch has to be rebased first, so those results would be stale.

## Review lessons

- **"Review against current main" applies.** I checked conflicts with `merge-tree`, but the merged result can't be built until the conflicts are resolved.
- **"Test a guard by planting a violation" is satisfied.** The roundtrip assertion fails on the pre-fix writer.
- **No other lesson fits.** There's no trail to read.

**Proposed new lesson for `General.md`** (I'll only add it once you approve this text):
> When a change tightens how something is parsed, update the code that writes that input in the same PR and add a test that writes and then reads it back. A stricter reader on its own turns valid writes into silent misses.

## Where the PR stands

- **CI:** no checks are attached. Five workflow runs for `ef07a954a` started Sep 17 and ended Oct 17 as "failure" with zero jobs. That most likely means they waited for a maintainer to approve the fork's workflows and expired after 30 days. As far as I know, GitHub won't start new pull-request runs while the PR has merge conflicts.
- **Reviews:** none, with no comments or threads. A review is requested from @entireio/cli-maintainers. Last activity was Sep 17.
- **Mergeability:** conflicting. #2253 is in the same state: conflicting, no checks, no reviews.
- **Entire trail:** none for #2259 or #2253.

## Not this PR's bugs (possible follow-ups)

- **Amend with `commit -v`:** the restore-trailer-on-amend path (`manual_commit_hooks.go:662` here, `:859` on main) appends the trailer after git's comment block. In `commit -v --amend` that lands below the scissors line, and git deletes everything below it. I confirmed git's file layout but didn't run this through Entire's hook end to end.
- **For #2253's review:** its reader accepts a message whose only line is `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`. Git rejects that, because it never treats the subject paragraph as trailers.

## Recommended next steps (each waits for your go-ahead)

1. Decide whether to fold #2259 into #2253 or keep them stacked. I recommend folding: #2253 alone ships the mismatch, reviewers already see the combined diff, and you'd only rebase once.
2. Rebase #2253 onto main. Drop the changes to `manual_commit_migration.go`, which main deleted. Merge the `trailers.go` changes with main's `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` and `HasOPFApplied`, and move the attach edits into `attach_confirm.go`. Then add the writer change as one squashed commit that explains the `#` decision.
3. Re-run the before/after check and `mise run check` on the rebased tree.
4. Rewrite the PR description and close or update issue #2256 to match.
5. Push only after you approve, then ask a maintainer to approve the fork's workflow runs.

Hand-over notes are saved in the shared notes folder as `pr-2259-trailer-writer.md`.

Forged `Entire-Checkpoint` lines in commit bodies can select and mutate unrelated checkpoints [OPEN]
## Summary

Checkpoint resolution parses trailers out of the whole commit message, including in code paths that decide whether to create, reuse, or mutate checkpoint storage. A line shaped like `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` anywhere in the body is indistinguishable from a real squashed trailer. So a commit body that names an existing checkpoint ID, whether pasted, reverted, or written by someone else, gets treated as authority over that checkpoint.

## Impact

A commit body naming an existing checkpoint ID can:

- make PostCommit condensation bind the commit to a checkpoint that has nothing to do with it, instead of minting a fresh one
- make `entire checkpoint attach` write the attached session into the unrelated checkpoint
- make `entire checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` persist a generated summary into it via `store.Write`
- make legacy session migration (`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`) advance `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` off a body ID, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution

Checking that the ID exists in storage doesn't help. Existence proves nothing about the ID's relationship to this commit.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Work in a repo with Entire enabled, in an agent session that has already produced at least one checkpoint. Note an existing checkpoint ID from `entire checkpoint list` (call it `<unrelated-id>`).
2. Make an unrelated code change in a new agent session.
3. Commit it with a message whose body contains a checkpoint-shaped line naming the existing ID:

   ```sh
   git commit -m "innocent change

   Entire-Checkpoint: <unrelated-id>"
   ```

4. Let the PostCommit hook run, then inspect `entire checkpoint list` and the commit's linkage.

**Expected:** the body line is ignored. The commit gets a fresh checkpoint for the new session's work.

**Actual:** the parser picks up `<unrelated-id>` from the body and condensation binds the commit to that unrelated checkpoint. The same forged line steers `attach`, `explain --generate`, and legacy migration, since they resolve IDs through the same whole-message parse.

The indented variant also works, even though Git itself doesn't consider it a trailer: `  Entire-Checkpoint: <unrelated-id>` (leading whitespace) is left-trimmed before classification and accepted, while `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns nothing for the same message.

## Root cause

One parser answers two different questions.

Discovery asks which checkpoints a commit's history mentions. Scanning the whole message is correct there, because GitHub and native squash commits embed several checkpoint trailers in the body.

Authorization asks which checkpoint an operation may mutate. Only the final trailer block can answer that, and the parser never made the distinction.

The parser is also looser than Git's own trailer grammar, which widens the hole. Besides the indentation issue above, commit-message-file cleanup hard-codes `#` instead of honoring `core.commentChar`.

## Suggested fix

Split the parser in two. Keep whole-message parsing for read-only discovery only (squash-history resume, listing), so commits with several embedded trailers keep working. Add a strict parser that reads only the final trailer block and matches Git's grammar: no leading whitespace, comment-char-aware cleanup. Route every mutation decision through the strict parser: commit hooks, attach, `explain --generate`, and legacy migration reconciliation. When the recorded commit hash is unavailable in migration, decline reconciliation rather than trusting body text.

Related: #2168 covers broader trailer-line anchoring and doesn't overlap with this.

func zzAttachForged(t *testing.T, commitMessage string) {
	t.Helper()
	setupAttachTestRepo(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	forgedCheckpointID := id.MustCheckpointID("a1b2c3d4e5f6")

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(mustGetwd(t))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	store := cpkg.NewGitStore(repo, cpkg.DefaultV1Refs())
	require.NoError(t, store.Write(ctx, cpkg.Session{

		Strategy:     "manual-commit",
		Transcript:   redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte("unrelated transcript\n")),
		AuthorName:   "Test",
		AuthorEmail:  "test@example.com",
	}))

	repoDir := mustGetwd(t)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, repoDir, "forged.txt", "forged")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, repoDir, "forged.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, repoDir, commitMessage)

	const attachedSessionID = "test-attach-unauthorized-checkpoint"
	setupClaudeTranscript(t, attachedSessionID, `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"hello"},"uuid":"u1"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"uuid":"a1"}
`)

	var out bytes.Buffer
	require.NoError(t, runAttach(ctx, &out, &out, attachedSessionID, agent.AgentNameClaudeCode, attachOptions{Force: true}))
	t.Logf("attach output:\n%s", out.String())

	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)

	repo, err = git.PlainOpen(repoDir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	store = cpkg.NewGitStore(repo, cpkg.DefaultV1Refs())

	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Logf("LastCheckpointID=%s forged checkpoint sessions=%d", state.LastCheckpointID, len(forgedSummary.Sessions))
	require.NotEqual(t, forgedCheckpointID, state.LastCheckpointID,
		"unauthorized checkpoint text must not select the write target")
	require.Len(t, forgedSummary.Sessions, 1, "unrelated checkpoint must not gain the attached session")
}

Yes, #2253 still adds real protection on top of main, mostly for `attach` and for commits whose message names a checkpoint ID. But it should be rebuilt on main's new code rather than rebased commit by commit.

**How I checked:** I exported current main (`a334cb698`) into a scratch folder, ported #2253's test scenarios to main's APIs, and ran them there. Nothing in the repo or worktree changed. In each case below, a "forged" ID means an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` line in the commit body rather than in the final trailer block.

| Scenario | Main today | With #2253 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`attach`** on a commit whose message names another checkpoint | **Writes the attached session into that unrelated checkpoint**, which ends up with 2 sessions. Fails for a body line, an indented line, and even a mid-sentence mention ("Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: …"), because main's matcher isn't anchored to the start of a line. | Only the final trailer block counts, so a fresh checkpoint is used |
| **PostCommit**, forged ID that is *not* in the local store | **Writes the session's work under that ID**, for example a teammate's checkpoint that hasn't been fetched yet | Ignored |
| **PostCommit**, forged ID that *does* exist locally | Correctly refuses to write there (main's new provenance check), **but the commit then gets no checkpoint at all** | The commit gets a fresh checkpoint |
| **prepare-commit-msg** with a forged body line | Treats it as "already stamped" and adds no fresh trailer, which causes the previous row | Stamps a fresh trailer |
| **`explain --commit … --generate`** | Still takes the first match anywhere in the message. I read this in the code but didn't test it. Low harm: it summarizes the wrong checkpoint. | Fixed |
| **Legacy migration** | That code no longer exists on main | Drop this part of #2253 |
| **Comment character** | Main still hard-codes `#` | #2253 adds `core.commentChar` support, but the [pr-2253](#local_4667db20-fe47-430d-86b3-b1f651542a0b) review found its `auto` detection picks the wrong character with real git |

**What main already covers:** it won't write new work into a checkpoint that already exists locally and that this session didn't stamp, and it handles squash-inherited trailers. #2253 overlaps with that part only.

**What this means for #2253:**
- **Keep:** the strict final-block parser, plus #2259's writer fix. Route it through main's new decision points instead of the old ones: `resolveCheckpointID` (attach), `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg), `stampedTrailersOf` (PostCommit), and the explain commit path.
- **Drop:** the migration changes.
- **Fix or split out:** the comment-character handling.
- **Be careful with squash commits.** Main deliberately reads trailers inherited from squash merges out of the whole message, so those whole-message reads must stay.

Because #2253 is still needed, my earlier recommendation holds: fold #2259 into it during that rebuild. The code change is a handful of call sites; most of the work is rewriting the tests against main's current helpers.

Here's the rebuild plan for #2253. Nothing has been edited, committed or pushed. Closing #2259 with a comment is the last step, and I'll show you the comment text before posting it.

## Brief

**Problem.** On current main, an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` line in a commit *body* still counts as permission to write to that checkpoint. I confirmed three cases with tests:
- `attach` writes the session into an unrelated checkpoint.
- PostCommit writes new work under an ID that isn't in the local store.
- prepare-commit-msg treats a body line as "already stamped", so the commit can end up with no checkpoint.

**Root cause.** Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers from the whole message, using a pattern that isn't anchored to the line start. Main's new provenance check only covers one case: a checkpoint that already exists locally.

**Change.** Only the final trailer block grants permission to write. Read-only lookups (resume, status, history, squash discovery) keep reading the whole message. Writing a trailer uses exactly the same rule (#2259's fix).

## Where it changes (main's current code)

| Area | Change | Stays as is, and why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trailers.go` | One strict final-block rule (`isTrailerBlock`) shared by reader and writer, plus `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock` / `ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`. `HasOPFApplied` uses it too: an indented OPF line stops counting, which only triggers extra redaction, the safe direction. | `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` stays broad on purpose, since deletion should remove every copy |
| `manual_commit_provenance.go` | `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (PostCommit) switch to the final block | `withoutInherited` / `withoutDeletedCheckpoints` logic unchanged |
| `manual_commit_hooks.go` | New helper that cleans a commit message the way git will before reading it: cut at the `-v` scissors line, and drop `#` lines for editor-written messages. `handleAmendCommitMsg` uses it, so an amend still keeps its real trailer. | Squash `SQUASH_MSG` reading and the "already present" checks stay whole-message, because squashed messages are indented. `CommitMsg` is unchanged. |
| `attach.go` | `planAttachLink` (`:686`) and `resolveCheckpointID` (`:1370`) switch together. A body mention then leads to the amend path with a fresh trailer instead of joining someone else's checkpoint. | |
| `explain.go` | The `--generate` paths (`:637`, `:2771`) use the final block. Read-only explain keeps whole-message discovery. | |
| Dropped from old #2253 | The legacy migration changes (that code is gone from main) and the comment-character detection (buggy) | |
| Docs | One paragraph in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` next to the inherited-trailer section | |

## Tests first (your rule), each confirmed failing on main before any production code

1. **Trailer rules (unit tests in `trailers_test.go`).**
   - Cases: a body line above the final block, indented or tab-indented lines, continuation lines, several final trailers, a message whose subject is the only trailer (rejected, matching git).
   - Writer round trip: every message the writer produces must be one the reader accepts (from #2259).
   - An indented OPF line doesn't count as applied.
2. **Hook flow, end to end.** These go in main's adversarial suite, `integration_test/rewrite_adversarial_test.go`, which drives the real prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hook binaries. Each `-m` case should get a fresh checkpoint and leave the named ID alone:
   - a body line naming an ID not in the local store
   - a body line naming another session's existing checkpoint
   - an indented body line
   - the agent (no-terminal) path

   Guard cases that must keep passing: an amend in the editor, with and without `-v`, keeps its trailer; the existing squash tests.
3. **Attach.** The three tests I already ran against main (body line, indented, mid-sentence), plus the existing tests for joining a real trailer.
4. **Explain.** `--commit X --generate` with only a body mention should error instead of generating; read-only explain should still find trailers in squash bodies.

## Steps

1. Create a fresh worktree with `worktree feature --branch checkpoint-trailer-authority --base main --remote upstream --apply`. I dry-ran it; it also fast-forwards your `main` worktree, which is clean apart from an untracked `.entire/graph-agent.md`. The #2253 worktree and its `progress.md` / `review.md` stay untouched.
2. Write the tests above and confirm they fail on main.
3. Implement in two commits:
   - `fix(trailers): read checkpoint authority from the final trailer block`, which includes #2259's writer change and the `#`-line reasoning
   - `fix(checkpoints): require the final trailer block before writing a checkpoint`
4. Verify:
   - `mise run fmt && mise run lint`, then `mise run test`, `mise run test:integration` and `mise run test:e2e:canary`
   - a throwaway random-message check against `git interpret-trailers`
   - your Review Lessons
5. Show you both commit messages before committing.
6. **Each of these needs your approval:**
   - (a) Force-push with `--force-with-lease` onto `origin/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`, which keeps PR #2253's number and its "Fixes #2255" link. The old head `7be8499d4` stays on your local branch.
   - (b) The new #2253 title and description, including "Fixes #2256", what main already covers, and the evidence.
   - (c) Closing #2259 with a comment. Draft text:
     > folding this into #2253, which i rebuilt on current main. the writer fix is the first commit there and #2256 is linked from it, so closing this one to keep a single PR to review.
   - (d) Asking a maintainer to approve the fork CI runs. No Trail is needed, since `work` creates none for fork PRs.

## Decisions (my recommendation in bold)

1. **Reuse #2253 by force-push**, rather than opening a new PR. Nobody has reviewed it, so nothing is lost.
2. **Split `core.commentChar` support into a follow-up.** It's a separate problem, #2253's version had bugs, and main hard-codes `#` everywhere today.
3. **Reject a message whose subject line is the only trailer**, as git does.
4. **Keep squash and redo carry-forward reading the whole message.** Those paths carry existing links forward, and GitHub squash commits keep trailers in the body.

**Known edge:** for `git commit -m … -e`, git labels the source "message" but still strips comments, so a trailer could be added twice. That's rare, and I'll note it in the PR.

**Related:** [entireio/cli#2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168), someone else's open fix for forged trailers in commit subjects, touches the same parser and may conflict. It doesn't block this.

Integration tests that run real git commands (e.g. `git rebase`) fire the test repo's installed hooks, which call `entire` from PATH, so they run `/opt/homebrew/bin/entire` (Homebrew cask `entireio/tap/entire@nightly`), not the test-built binary. When the installed nightly is older than main, its hooks can corrupt session state, e.g. delete it. On 2026-10-13 this made `TestManualCommit_MidSessionRebaseFollowsHead` and `TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork` fail locally while CI, which has no `entire` installed, passed.

**Why:** Hours were spent ruling out env vars, git config and ctime before finding this.
**How to apply:** If integration tests fail locally but pass on CI for the same SHA, first check `entire version` against main. Fix with `brew upgrade --cask entireio/tap/entire@nightly`, or put a fresh `go build ./cmd/entire` first on PATH.
